newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Sale of BBL stake not on agenda - GBL.
newsitem.headline: Sale of BBL stake not on agenda - GBL.

text.p: Belgian holding company Groupe Bruxelles Lambert (GBL) said on Tuesday the sale of its stake in bank Banque Bruxelles Lambert (BBL) was not on the agenda now.
It made the announcement at its annual shareholders' meeting.

"Our leaving BBL is not on the agenda," Gerald Frere, GBL co-chief executive officer, said. GBL had the support for this "development" from the other BBL shareholders (Belgian insurer Royale Belge and Belgian bank Dexia) with which it forms a BBL shareholders pact.
Frere reiterated that at the beginning of 1993 following the failed takeover bid on BBL by Dutch bancasurance group ING, GBL said that it wanted to stay in BBL for between five and seven years.
ING is still a significant BBL minority shareholder.

"We are convinced and the bank's management is convinced that BBL will achieve an excellent performance in the future so that it can position itself in the big market that will open very soon," he said.
GBL owns a direct stake of around 12.4 percent of BBL.
Royale Belge, GBL and Belgium's second largest bank Dexia CC together own around 37 percent of BBL, outvoting ING.
